title: main() reads env vars instead of the stdin JSON envelope + argv event name
plan_refs: plan L243 (§3.4 Plugin Executable Invocation), L1284-1360 (§11.1 envelope shape with top-level event/data/context)
code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender main() L5213-5236: reads HERDR_PLUGIN_EVENT, HERDR_PLUGIN_EVENT_JSON, HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON; never reads sys.stdin or argv[1]
required_change: Parse the event from stdin: read sys.stdin (bounded, non-blocking, within time_remaining()), json.loads it, take event_name = envelope.get('event') or argv[1] (argv[1] is the event name per the plan), data = envelope['data'], context = envelope['context']. If stdin is empty or malformed, fall back to argv ${1:-}: no-op for a known event name with no payload, or start background recovery (ensure_reconciler_running). Keep the env-var path only as a secondary fallback. Type-check envelope/data/context as dicts; treat non-dicts as {}. Add tests that run the binary as a subprocess with the §3.4 captured envelope on stdin, and with empty and malformed stdin.

title: Case C (omitted agent key) maps to Ended instead of Idle; Case B vs C is not distinguished
plan_refs: plan L164-173 (§2.2 Cases A/B/C), L249 (Agent Exit Signal), L1311-1323 fixtures
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2232-2255: `if not raw_agent and agent_status != "idle": raw_agent = cached_s.get("raw_agent")` and then the idle branch maps to Ended whenever raw_agent is falsy and a session exists
required_change: Classify idle events by key presence: has_agent_key = 'agent' in event_data; ev_agent = str(event_data.get('agent') or '').strip(). Case A: ev_agent non-empty -> Idle. Case B: has_agent_key and ev_agent == '' (null or empty) -> Ended, even when the pane is focused and context.focused_pane_agent is set (Case B must win over the §2.3 hierarchy). Case C: key absent -> if a cached session exists with raw_agent and desired_state != 'Ended', keep raw_agent and map to Idle; otherwise discard. Add unit tests for Case C (key omitted -> Idle with retained agent) and for Case B on a focused pane that has a stale focused_pane_agent.

title: A non-idle event with no agent revives an Ended (not yet evicted) session through the cached raw_agent
plan_refs: plan L157-163 (admission requires event agent, or focused agent, or an existing session with desired_state != Ended)
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2236-2244: raw_agent is filled from cached_s['raw_agent'] before the check `if cached_s.get('desired_state') == 'Ended': if not raw_agent: return`, so the Ended guard is bypassed
required_change: Run the admission check before the cached fallback: positive_signal = event agent non-empty after strip OR (is_focused and focused_pane_agent non-empty after strip). Admit only if positive_signal OR (session exists AND desired_state != 'Ended'). Apply the cached raw_agent fallback only for display-name resolution after admission. Add a test: Ended session still in cache plus 'working' with no agent -> no resurrection.

title: Admission does not strip whitespace from event.data.agent
plan_refs: plan L160 (non-empty after stripping whitespace), L99
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2236-2246 (`not raw_agent` truthiness); tombstone path L2205 does strip
required_change: Normalize ev_agent = str(event_data.get('agent') or '').strip() (same for focused_pane_agent) and use these stripped values for every admission and Case A/B decision.

title: Agent name is not stripped of ANSI/OSC/control characters or truncated to 64
code_refs: format_agent_name L1178-1183
required_change: In format_agent_name, run the raw agent through the same OSC/DCS/CSI/control stripping as sanitize_title (factor out a shared strip_terminal_controls()), then strip, lowercase, map through AGENT_NAME_OVERRIDES, and truncate the final string to 64 characters. Also handle non-str input with str(). Add tests with an OSC-injected agent name and a 200-character agent name.

title: cwd hierarchy order is wrong, and cwd is never sanitized or truncated
plan_refs: plan L188 (event.cwd -> cached cwd -> focused_pane_cwd if focused -> workspace_cwd if focused -> ''; control-strip; 256 chars)

Apply CONTROL_REGEX stripping (plus CSI/OSC stripping) and truncate to 256 characters; coerce non-str to str. Add tests for focused-pane precedence (cached beats focused) and for control-character and length sanitization.

title: tab_id and workspace_id resolved in status events are not validated against the container regex
plan_refs: plan L189-190 (validated against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_:-]{1,48}$; null/'' if invalid)
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2244-2270 (event_data workspace_id and tab_id stored as given)
required_change: After resolution, set tab_id = tab_id if isinstance(tab_id, str) and CONTAINER_ID_REGEX.match(tab_id) else None, and do the same for workspace_id with '' as the fallback. Invalid values must fall through to the next hierarchy level, not be stored. Add tests with an invalid tab_id or workspace_id.

title: An event workspace_id that disagrees with the colon-qualified pane prefix is stored, which makes workspace.closed cleanup wrong
plan_refs: plan L190 (hierarchy lists event.data.workspace_id first, yet also says a colon-qualified pane is used directly 'without workspace prefixing or override'); L11
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2156-2172, L2268-2269 (also special-cases workspace_id == 'default')
required_change: Recommended reading: when canonical_pane contains ':', the workspace_id stored in cache must equal its prefix. The canonical pane identity is authoritative, and a mismatched event workspace_id should be logged and ignored. Otherwise workspace.closed for the prefix workspace misses the session, and a close of the wrong workspace evicts it. Also remove the `workspace_id == "default"` special case (the plan says never fall back to 'default'). Amend plan §2.3 so the prefix takes precedence over event.data.workspace_id when the pane is colon-qualified.

title: Sanitized hostname is not truncated to 32 characters, and session_id is never checked against the 96-character bound
plan_refs: plan L15, L185 (re.sub(...)[:32], fallback 'local', total ^[a-zA-Z0-9_:-]{1,96}$), L116 (salvage regex host {1,32})
code_refs: get_sanitized_hostname L94-97; session_id built at L2177-2179 with no validation; SESSION_ID_REGEX L50 used in salvage
required_change: Return (clean[:32] or 'local'). Validate the pinned data['host'] read from cache against ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ and fall back to get_sanitized_hostname() if it fails. After building session_id, assert it matches ^[a-zA-Z0-9_:-]{1,96}$ and SESSION_ID_REGEX, and log and reject if not. Without the truncation, hosts longer than 32 characters produce session IDs that corrupt-cache salvage can never recover (SESSION_ID_REGEX caps the host at 32). The code also splits on '.' before sanitizing, which the plan formula does not (the plan formula gives 'macbook-prolocal', the code gives 'macbook-pro'). Recommend keeping the split and updating the plan formula to `raw_host.split('.')[0]`, because the §11.2 fixture 'herdr:macbook:...' implies the split. Add a unit test that monkeypatches socket.gethostname to a 60-character name.

title: normalize_pane_id ignores HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID; the plan contradicts itself on env fallback
plan_refs: plan L13 (ws = workspace_id or os.environ.get('HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID')), L190, L249 vs L10 ('colon-less pane IDs without workspace_id in event data are invalid and rejected')
code_refs: normalize_pane_id L1186-1191; handle_agent_status_changed L2160-2162 and handle_pane_closed L2580-2582 reject before normalize can consult env
required_change: Pick one rule. Recommended: follow L13/L190/L249, stated three times, and make normalize_pane_id use `ws = workspace_id or os.environ.get('HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID')`, returning '' if empty. Have the handlers call normalize_pane_id and reject only when it returns '' instead of pre-rejecting. Edit L10 to read 'without workspace_id in event data or HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID'. Update parity tests 31/37 to clear or set HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID explicitly, because the ('pane123', None, '') case depends on the env being unset.

title: touch_pane_marker writes a second alias marker using a 'default' workspace fallback
plan_refs: plan L14 ('no alias, no symlink, and no dual-linking'), L190 ('never falling back to "default"'), L249
code_refs: touch_pane_marker L734-739 (alt_id = f"{HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID or 'default'}:{raw_pane_id}")
required_change: Remove the alt_id/hex_ids alias logic and write only panes/<hex(canonical_pane)>. Drop the unused raw_pane_id parameters from the touch_pane_marker, touch_pane_failed, clear_pane_failed, remove_pane_marker and cleanup_vendor_active signatures, or ignore them explicitly. Add a test asserting exactly one marker file after a confirmed delivery for a colon-less raw pane.

title: pane.closed falls back to the focused pane id and an unfocused context.workspace_id, and crashes when pane_id is missing
plan_refs: plan L181 (background events NEVER inherit focused workspace attributes), L190, L151
code_refs: handle_pane_closed L2576-2582: raw_pane = event_data.pane_id or context.focused_pane_id; workspace_id = event_data.workspace_id or context.workspace_id (no focus gate); `":" in raw_pane` raises TypeError when both are None; same raw_pane fallback in handle_agent_status_changed L2149
required_change: Require event_data['pane_id'] (a non-empty str) and return with a log line if it is absent. Never substitute focused_pane_id: a close or status event without pane_id must not act on the focused pane. Resolve workspace only from event_data.workspace_id (or HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID, per the normalize-env-fallback decision), never from an unfocused context.workspace_id, otherwise a colon-less background pane resolves into the focused workspace. Add tests: pane.closed without pane_id is a no-op; a background colon-less pane.closed does not use context.workspace_id.

title: tab.closed and workspace.closed use loose matching that can evict sessions in other containers
plan_refs: plan L152 ('every session where cached tab_id matches closed tab'), L153 ('cached workspace_id matches')
code_refs: handle_tab_closed L2738: `s_tab == tab_id or tab_id.endswith(str(s_tab))` (closing 'w11:t1' matches cached 'w1:t1'); handle_workspace_closed L2887: `f":{workspace_id}:" in sid` (a workspace named the same as the host, e.g. 'macbook', matches every session); both fall back to context ids when focused_pane_id is set
required_change: Use exact equality only: info.get('tab_id') == tab_id, and info.get('workspace_id') == workspace_id or info['pane_id'].split(':',1)[0] == workspace_id. Remove the context fallback for container ids, since a close event without its id should be a no-op. Add regression tests: 'w11:t1' does not close 'w1:t1', and workspace.closed with a workspace id equal to the host does not close other workspaces.

title: Ended payloads from close handlers omit terminal, event and seq
plan_refs: plan L191-193 (terminal 'Herdr', event = source event name sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9.] max 64, seq = transmitting_seq), L119 (the minimal 3-field payload is only the retry fallback)
code_refs: handle_pane_closed L2644, handle_tab_closed L2793, handle_workspace_closed L2941: {'state','agent','session_id'} only
required_change: Build close payloads as {'state':'Ended','agent':...,'session_id':sid,'title','cwd' (from cache),'terminal':'Herdr','event':<'pane.closed'|'tab.closed'|'workspace.closed'>,'seq':seq}. Keep the 3-field minimal payload only for the single fallback retry. Add a sanitize_event_name() helper (re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9.]','',name)[:64]) and use it for every payload's 'event' field.

title: Unrecognized agent_status is silently ignored without the required warning
plan_refs: plan L150 (log warning to plugin.log; do not mutate cache)
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2251-2253 (`if not mapped_state: return` with no log)
required_change: Validate agent_status up front, before the cache lock and before tombstone or agent_exits handling: if it is not in STATUS_MAP and not 'unknown', call log_debug(f'Warning: unrecognized agent_status {agent_status!r} for pane {canonical_pane}') and return. Add a test that checks the log line and that the cache is unchanged.

title: Title/ANSI stripping misses CSI sequences with private or intermediate bytes
plan_refs: plan L187 (stripped of all ANSI CSI, OSC, DCS and control characters)
code_refs: CSI_REGEX L44 `\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]`; verified that '\x1b[?25hHi\x1b[>4;2m!' sanitizes to '[?25hHi[>4;2m!'
required_change: Use the ECMA-48 form: CSI_REGEX = r'(\x1b\[|\x9b)[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]'. Make OSC and DCS also accept the 8-bit introducers (\x9d, \x90) and an unterminated tail up to the end of the string. Use the shared helper for title, agent and cwd. Add tests with private-mode CSI and OSC-8 hyperlinks.

title: Corrupt-cache salvage re-pins host to the current hostname instead of the host recovered from salvaged session ids

code_refs: BoundedSessionCache._load salvage return L1084-1094 ('host': get_sanitized_hostname()) while the salvaged sessions use parts[1]
required_change: When salvaged sessions exist, set the root host to the most common parts[1] among salvaged ids (when it is valid), so that later events map to the same session_id as the salvaged records.

title: Context-isolation and parity tests do not exercise the risky paths
code_refs: run_unit_tests test 18 L3406-3418 (the event supplies agent 'claude', so focused-agent leakage is never tested); tests 31/37 L3837-3866, L4160-4185 re-implement the bash derivation inline instead of executing HOOK_GUARD_TEMPLATE's own lines; no test for Case C, Ended resurrection, hostname truncation, agent/cwd sanitization, tab_id validation, or a missing pane_id
required_change: Test 18: a background event with no agent and focused_pane_agent 'codex' must not be admitted (and must not take Codex as its agent if a session exists). Parity tests: extract the canonical/hex block from HOOK_GUARD_TEMPLATE (between markers) and run that exact text, or have the guard echo _HB_HEX_PANE in a debug mode. Add the missing cases listed in the other gaps. All tests must use a temp HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME and HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR so --unit-test never writes into the real $HOME.

title: The focused-agent admission clause uses a different focus test than §2.3
plan_refs: plan L161 (focused_pane_id == canonical_pane_id) vs L181 (is_focused = focused_id in (canonical_pane, raw_pane))
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2169 (uses the §2.3 form for both purposes)
required_change: Recommend the §2.3 form as normative, since Herdr context may report the raw form, and amending L161 to reference is_focused. The code needs no change; only the plan text.

title: Cache lock 'acquisition' proceeds WITHOUT the lock on contention (no mutual exclusion)
plan_refs: plan L390-391 (Step A LOCK_NB with deadline, contention => spool and exit), L482-483 (Step C lock failure => results envelope and exit)
code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender BoundedSessionCache.__enter__ L911-927: on timeout it logs 'proceeding with best effort', sets IN_CRITICAL_SECTION=True and returns self._load() anyway; every handler then does read-modify-write + save() unlocked
required_change: __enter__ must report failure (raise a LockTimeout or return a sentinel) when flock is not obtained within deadline min(0.2, max(0.02, time_remaining()-0.3)). Callers in Step A must then enqueue_spool(...) + ensure_reconciler_running() and exit 0; callers in Step C must write_result_envelope(...) and exit; background/reconciler callers should block (or retry with their own longer budget). __exit__ must only LOCK_UN if acquired. Add a multi-process test that holds the flock in a child and asserts (a) the handler spools instead of writing the cache, (b) a Step C failure produces a results/ file.

title: break/continue inside the locked Step C block skips ALL post-lock dispatch (compensation send, orphan I/O, reconciler spawn, vendor cleanup)
plan_refs: plan L294-298, L489-496 (stale-send compensation sent outside lock), L498-503 (lease mismatch => ensure_reconciler_running), L505-510, L519-528 (Ended eviction => orphan removal + vendor cleanup), L561-567 (post-lock external dispatch)
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed: break at L2421 (stale-send compensation staged then loop exits before the `if compensation_needed:` block at ~L2523), L2430 (lease superseded; should_spawn_reconciler set but ensure_reconciler_running never called), L2440 (resync superseded, same), L2481 (Ended confirmed: orphans_to_remove and vendor_to_clean never executed). handle_pane_closed: continue at L2654 and L2663 skip ensure_reconciler_running (L2709+)
required_change: Restructure so the with-block only sets flags/staged lists and the post-lock dispatch section always runs after the lock is released (e.g. set `done=True` instead of break, exit the with, run dispatch, then `if done: break`). Compensating Ended must be sent synchronously when budget allows; ensure_reconciler_running must be called whenever should_spawn_reconciler is set; orphan removal and vendor cleanup must run after Ended eviction. Replace hollow tests #43/#48 (which re-implement the logic inline) with tests that drive the real handler through a delayed mock POST concurrent with handle_pane_closed and assert the bridge received the compensating Ended and that pending_compensations is cleared.

title: Persisted compensation is removed from pending_compensations BEFORE the compensating send (and even when deferred for budget)
plan_refs: plan L486 (record under lock; after successful dispatch re-acquire lock to clear entry; reconciler drains on SIGALRM/exit), L562-564
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed ~L2518-2549: re-verification lock clears data['pending_compensations'] then sends; when time_remaining()<=0.3 it only touches reconciler.pending after having already deleted the entry. reconcile_active_sessions L1486-1507 has the same clear-then-send order
required_change: Keep the entry until the compensating POST has returned; clear it in the post-send re-lock (the same lock that performs post-compensation re-sync detection). When budget-deferred, leave the entry in place. On abort due to re-admitted live session, clear it under that lock. Same fix in reconcile_active_sessions.

title: Step A contention spooling never happens; enqueue_spool is dead code in production
plan_refs: plan L391 (write envelope to spool/<enqueued_ns:020d>_<pid>_<monotonic_ns>.json, cap 100 protecting closes, spawn --reconcile-background, exit)
code_refs: enqueue_spool L1301 is only called from unit tests (L3246-3388); no handler calls it; enqueue_spool itself does not spawn the helper
required_change: Wire enqueue_spool into the Step A lock-failure path of every handler (status, pane/tab/workspace closed) and have it (or the caller) call ensure_reconciler_running(). Set enqueued_ns = time.time_ns() as specified (keep arrival_ns separately; see plan-contradiction note) and name the file by it, or amend the plan to name by arrival_ns.

title: Live Step A does not replay the spool under lock; replay only happens in the reconciler via full handlers with network I/O
plan_refs: plan L393-403 (Step A: drain up to 16 envelopes FIFO under the lock, close admission ordering, tombstone recording, status staleness, unlink only after save)
code_refs: replay_spool_dir L1412-1452 is called only from run_reconcile_background L1822; it invokes handle_* per envelope (each doing its own lock cycles and HTTP POSTs), so it is neither a pure under-lock mutation nor bounded by the <10ms CPU lock budget
required_change: Factor a pure `apply_envelope_locked(data, envelope)` that performs the cache mutation only (close: admission check arrival_ns>=admitted_at_ns and generation if present, tombstone dict, desired_state=Ended, seq++; status: source-ts or arrival vs last_event_ns supersession) and call it from Step A of the live handler for up to 16 files before evaluating the live event, unlinking each file after the save. Delivery of replayed sessions is then done by the universal sender/reconciler. Add schema validation (event_name in known set, event_data dict, arrival_ns int) that quarantines to spool/bad. Remove or gate the non-spec 'direct_post' event type (test-only).

title: is_disabled() is not re-checked under the lock in Step A or Step C
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2180+ and Step C ~L2405; handle_pane_closed L2593 and L2650; only main() L5207 checks before dispatch
required_change: Immediately after acquiring the lock in Step A and Step C of every handler, `if is_disabled(): return` without saving or sending.

title: Results directory: never written by handlers; drain uses a schema different from the plan and applies wrong state transitions
plan_refs: plan L483 (envelope fields version:1, session_id, transmitting_seq, transmitting_state, status success|non_retryable|retryable, error, timestamp_ns, pid; drain applies confirmations with staleness check transmitting_seq >= delivered_seq)
code_refs: write_result_envelope L1348 (no caller outside tests); drain_results_dir L1369-1409 reads 'success'/'is_non_retryable'/'pane_id' instead of 'status'; requires s.seq == r_seq (discards valid older confirmations); maps non-retryable to 'retryable_exhausted' and retryable to 'in_flight' without rejected_seq/delivery_attempts; Ended success evicts without recording tombstone/agent_exits, orphan removal or vendor cleanup; compensation staged with generation 1/admitted_at_ns 0/agent 'Herdr'
required_change: Have Step C lock-failure write the plan's envelope (also include pane_id and agent for compensation). In drain: parse 'status'; on success apply if transmitting_seq >= delivered_seq (evict only if Ended and seq == transmitting_seq, recording tombstone/agent_exits from persisted session origins, staging orphan removal and pending_vendor_cleanups); on non_retryable set non_retryable_failed + rejected_seq + .failed marker + orphan export for Ended; on retryable increment delivery_attempts and apply the 5-attempt exhaustion rule; stage compensation with the real agent and pane_generations[pane]. Add tests for each status.

title: 256 cap rejects session 257 without first pruning Ended/salvaged sessions
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2233-2235 rejects when len(sessions)>=256; save() L1117-1129 prunes only when len>256 (never reached) and only 'safe' Ended (delivered/orphaned) or salvaged
required_change: At admission, when the pane is new and len(sessions)>=256, prune Ended sessions and salvaged records (oldest last_event_at first; for undelivered Ended export as orphan first to preserve zero-data-loss) and reject only if still >=256 live sessions. Extend test #51 to fill with e.g. 255 live + 1 Ended and assert 257th admission succeeds.

title: pane.closed does not persist closed_source_ts on the session; Step C overwrites the tombstone with closed_source_ts=0.0
plan_refs: plan L264 (closed_at_ns recorded once, stable origin), L278, L451 (persist closed_at_ns and closed_source_ts on session), L528 (tombstone re-affirmed from persisted session origins)
code_refs: handle_pane_closed L2602-2606 writes a correct tombstone, L2619 sets info['closed_at_ns']=arr_ns (overwriting any earlier close) but never info['closed_source_ts']; on success L2684-2688 rewrites the tombstone with s.get('closed_source_ts', 0.0)=0.0, weakening the positive-admission source check (src_ts > 0 trivially true)
required_change: In Step A of pane close set info['closed_source_ts'] = the computed closed_source_ts and only set closed_at_ns/closed_source_ts if not already present for the current generation (setdefault) so duplicate/delayed closes keep the original origin; likewise do not overwrite an existing tombstone's closed_at_ns. Add a test asserting tombstone closed_source_ts survives Step C confirmation.

title: pane.closed records a tombstone even when the close predates the current session admission
plan_refs: plan L398 (discard close events predating admission), L575 (cascade ignores closes predating admission)
code_refs: handle_pane_closed L2602 records tombstone unconditionally before the per-session admitted_at_ns check at L2614
required_change: Record/refresh the tombstone only when at least one matching session accepted the close (or no session exists and the close is not older than the pane's last admission); a stale replayed close must not tombstone a freshly admitted pane. Also save the tombstone even when sessions is empty (currently gated by `if sessions:` L2635) to keep behavior consistent.

title: Source staleness filter lacks the 0.1s tolerance and uses truthiness
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2288: `if source_ts and last_source_ts and source_ts < last_source_ts: return`
required_change: Use `if source_ts is not None and float(source_ts) < float(session.get('last_source_timestamp', 0)) - 0.1: drop`, evaluated before seq increment (already is). Add a test with a 50ms-older timestamp being accepted.

title: agent_exits entries are not pruned after 60s globally and are popped on 'working' without requiring event.data.agent
code_refs: BoundedSessionCache.save L1096-1166 prunes tombstones only; agent_exits pruned lazily at L2224 only when the same pane receives an event; L2229 pops on working without checking agent
required_change: Prune agent_exits entries with now_ns - exit_at_ns > 60s in save() alongside tombstones; require a non-empty event_data['agent'] before popping on a working event.

title: last_event_ns not clamped monotonic (plan self-contradictory)
plan_refs: plan L263 (last_event_ns = max(now_ns, prev+1)) vs L435 (session['last_event_ns'] = arr_ns)
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2310 and L2339 set last_event_ns = arr_ns
required_change: Recommend `last_event_ns = max(arr_ns, session.get('last_event_ns', 0) + 1)`: keeps the arrival basis used by §4.3 replay comparisons while guaranteeing strict monotonicity on equal/backward clocks. Keep last_arrival_ns as the raw arrival for ordering drops. Update §4.3 L435 to match.

title: Generation/admitted_at_ns re-bumped on every event while delivered_state=='Ended' but desired_state is live
plan_refs: plan L270, L441-446 (bump only on new admission or transitioning from Ended)
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2301 is_new_turn includes cached_s.get('delivered_state') == 'Ended'
required_change: Bump only when the record is new (no generation) or cached desired_state == 'Ended'. Otherwise repeated bumps move admitted_at_ns forward and cause legitimate spooled closes (arrival between admissions) to be discarded.

title: Synchronous Step B is not capped at 1 iteration / 2 POSTs (plan self-contradictory)
plan_refs: plan L471-472 (at most 1 session, at most 2 POST attempts, at most 1 iteration) vs L531 and L553-556 ('loop continues and transmits latest desired_state', 'continue loop to Step B')
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed while loop L2395-2571 iterates while time_remaining()>0.3; plus compensation POST and cleanup_vendor_active POST
required_change: Recommend the cap reading (L471): it is the only one that guarantees the 1.4s watchdog with 0.2s POSTs + lock waits. In the 'newer state arrived' branch, clear the lease, touch reconciler.pending and ensure_reconciler_running() instead of looping. Clarify in the plan that compensating Ended and vendor-dismiss POSTs are outside the 2-POST cap but subject to the time_remaining()>0.3 gate. Also gate the first POST on time_remaining()>0.3 (L472).

title: Minimal Ended retry is not budget-gated and socket timeout formula differs
plan_refs: plan L478-479 (timeout min(0.2, max(0.05, time_remaining()-0.3)); retry only if time_remaining()>0.3)

title: Reconciler-driven replays inherit the 1.4s per-process budget: lock deadline collapses to 20ms and every budget gate fails

code_refs: run_unit_tests #43 (L4340-4379) and #48 (L4463-4495) re-implement compensation logic inline rather than exercising Step C; no test for lock-contention spooling, results/ envelopes, Step A replay, is_disabled under lock, capacity pruning of Ended sessions, agent_exits pruning, closed_source_ts preservation; is_herdr_alive() returns True under HERDR_BARTENDER_UNIT_TESTING so condition 4 of positive admission is untestable; tests write into real $HOME state dir

title: Lock acquisition timeout proceeds without the lock instead of spooling
plan_refs: plan L390-391 (contention rule), §6.1 L700-705, budget table L713
code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender BoundedSessionCache.__enter__ L911-927; enqueue_spool L1301 (never called by any handler)
required_change: The deadline formula min(0.2, max(0.02, time_remaining()-0.3)) is correct. But when it runs out, __enter__ only logs 'proceeding with best effort', sets IN_CRITICAL_SECTION=True and returns _load(), so handle_tab_closed/handle_workspace_closed change and os.replace the cache without holding the flock, and concurrent writers can lose each other's updates. Fix: __enter__ must report the failure (raise LockContention or set self.acquired=False). Each handler, including both cascade handlers, must then call enqueue_spool(event_name, event_data, context, arrival_ns=arr_ns), call ensure_reconciler_running() and return. Blocking callers (--cleanup, the reconciler) may keep a longer or blocking wait. Add a test that holds the flock from a child process and checks that a spool envelope is written and the cache is not changed.

title: Orphan file lock is blocking LOCK_EX, not LOCK_NB with a 50ms deadline
plan_refs: §6.1 L703 (LOCK_NB, 50ms, delegate on contention); budget table L720 (10ms); §4.3 item 5 Post-Lock L608
code_refs: export_orphan_record L1215-1253 and remove_orphan_record L1256-1298 (fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)); called after Step C in handle_tab_closed/handle_workspace_closed
required_change: In the plugin event path, add a non_blocking/deadline parameter that loops on LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB for up to 50ms. On contention, return False and leave the record in cache: orphaned_ended stays True, plus a pending_orphan_export/pending_orphan_remove flag. Then touch_reconciler_pending() and ensure_reconciler_running(), and have the reconciler drain those flags. The blocking mode should remain only for --cleanup, --replay-orphans and the reconciler. Plan conflict: §4.3 (L565, L608) says only 'under dedicated lock' while §6.1 requires LOCK_NB with a 50ms limit. Recommend §6.1, because a blocking flock in a watchdog-bounded process can be held until SIGALRM, which loses the export.

title: Cascade network I/O ignores the time_remaining() > 0.3s skip rule, and the socket timeout formula differs
plan_refs: §5.2 L683-685; §6.1 L701, L704 (skip network when <=0.3s); budget table L715-718 (minimal retry only on rejection and only if >0.3s); §4.3 L566
code_refs: _raw_post_event L821-861 (eff_timeout = max(0.05, min(timeout, tr-0.3 if tr>0.4 else tr))); post_bartender_event L864-876; cleanup_vendor_active L751-791; handle_tab_closed Step B L2792, post-lock L2860-2865; handle_workspace_closed same
required_change: 1) Compute the timeout as exactly min(0.2, max(0.05, time_remaining()-0.3)). The current code returns up to 0.2s when remaining is in (0.3, 0.4], where the spec allows 0.05-0.1s. 2) Before each Step B POST, minimal-payload retry, compensating POST and cleanup_vendor_active in the cascade handlers, check time_remaining() > 0.3. If it fails, leave the session in_flight, touch_reconciler_pending() and ensure_reconciler_running(). 3) post_bartender_event should retry the minimal payload only after a rejection (is_non_retryable=True or ok:false), not after a timeout or connection error, and only when time_remaining() > 0.3. 4) cleanup_vendor_active should use the same formula and gate, and defer to the reconciler when the budget is spent. Note: time_remaining() never returns less than 0.1 (L108), so gates must compare against 0.3 and not test for <= 0.

title: ITIMER_REAL is armed at 1.4s, not the specified 1.5s
code_refs: PROCESS_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 1.4 (L24); arm_watchdog L137-144; time_remaining L105-108
required_change: Set PROCESS_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 1.5 to match the spec, or update the spec if the 100ms extra margin is intended. Also, START_TIME is taken at module load and not at interpreter start, so startup cost (including the ps fork for PROCESS_START_TIME at L76) is not counted against the budget. Consider moving the PROCESS_START_TIME fork to lazy evaluation.

title: Deferred watchdog exit is checked only in save(), not in __exit__, and skips the reconciler handoff
plan_refs: §6.1 L727-729 (exit deferred until __exit__ completes swap and releases lock, then exit 0; outside critical sections launch reconciler if unconfirmed sessions remain)
code_refs: _timeout_watchdog L111-134; BoundedSessionCache.__exit__ L929-937; save() finally L1160-1164
required_change: Move the PENDING_WATCHDOG_EXIT check into __exit__, after LOCK_UN and close. Before sys.exit(0), call ensure_reconciler_running() when unconfirmed sessions remain. With-blocks that never call save() (Step C 'if not s: continue', --status/--sessions, a cascade where 'sessions' is empty, and _load raising) currently ignore the pending exit. Because the timer is one-shot, the process then runs network I/O with no deadline. save() also clears IN_CRITICAL_SECTION while the lock is still held, so later mutations in the same block are unprotected. Add tests that call _timeout_watchdog with IN_CRITICAL_SECTION=True and check that SystemExit(0) is raised only after the lock is released (a child process can then flock LOCK_NB).

title: Corrupt-load path can raise UnboundLocalError and leave the lock and IN_CRITICAL_SECTION stuck
plan_refs: §6.3 L737-783 (quarantine and salvage must always yield a fresh cache)
code_refs: _load L1020-1093: salvage_epoch_gen is defined inside the inner try at L1026, but L1090 uses it unconditionally
required_change: If the raw re-read fails (file removed between exists() and open, EACCES, and so on), the inner try swallows the error and the return statement then raises UnboundLocalError. That exception leaves __enter__ with IN_CRITICAL_SECTION=True and the flock fd still open, because __exit__ is never called. Initialise salvage_epoch_gen = max(int(time.time()), 1_700_000_000) before any try. Wrap __enter__ so a _load failure releases the lock and resets IN_CRITICAL_SECTION.

title: Salvaged cache is not written atomically under the held lock
code_refs: _load L1078-1093 returns the salvaged dict after moving the corrupt file but never saves; callers --status L5174, --sessions L5208 and early-return paths do not save
required_change: After building the salvaged dict in _load, call self.save(salvaged_data) or an internal _write_atomic while the lock is still held, so the salvage survives read-only callers. Today 'herdr-bartender --status' on a corrupt cache quarantines the file and drops every salvaged session. Add a test that runs a read-only with-block on a corrupt cache and then checks that the next load still contains the salvaged sessions.

title: No 7-day prune of active-sessions.json.corrupt.* files
code_refs: _load L1080-1081 (rename only); no other code matches 'corrupt.'
required_change: After the rename, glob state_dir/'active-sessions.json.corrupt.*' and unlink files whose mtime, or whose integer suffix, is older than 7*86400 seconds. Add a unit test using an injected clock or os.utime.

code_refs: BoundedSessionCache.__init__ L897-909 (sweeps only .guard_stdin.*); save L1152-1157 (a tmp file left after a write error is never removed)
required_change: In __init__ or at startup, also unlink state_dir/'active-sessions.json.tmp.*' (and spool/*.json.tmp, plus orphan .tmp.*) when mtime is more than 60s old. In save(), unlink tmp_path in the except branch. Add a test.

title: No 0.5s cache for get_bartender_pid / is_herdr_alive / start-time lookups
code_refs: get_bartender_pid L1455-1477 (pgrep plus ps per PID, on every _raw_post_event L827); get_herdr_pid L174-210; is_process_instance_alive L157-164 (ps fork per lease check inside the Step A critical section of both cascade handlers)

Separately, get_bartender_pid passes the already-epoch string from get_process_start_time to strptime again, which always fails, so it silently falls back to the lowest PID. Compare float(st) instead. Add a test that counts subprocess.run calls.

title: Cascade writes the tombstone only when this process claims the lease
plan_refs: §4.3 item 5 L577 (record tombstone for each matching session before the lease check); L91
code_refs: handle_tab_closed L2753-2767 (tombstone inside 'if not is_active'); handle_workspace_closed equivalent (W31-37)
required_change: Write data['tombstones'][pane_id] (and in tab.closed, info['closed_source_ts']) for every matching session before the lease check. Without this, a session whose lease is held by another live sender gets no tombstone, and a delayed pre-close status event can bring it back. Add a test where the lease is held by a live foreign PID and a later stale status event must be rejected.

title: Overflow lease clearing uses a second lock/save cycle instead of one Step A transaction
plan_refs: §4.3 item 5 L571 ('Step A acquires lock once'), L581-586; §6.1 L705 (left in_flight under cache lock)

required_change: Do the [:1]/[1:] split inside the first with-block: for overflow sessions set sending_pid, lease_token and lease_deadline to None and delivery_status='in_flight' before the single save. Then call touch_reconciler_pending() and ensure_reconciler_running() once, after the lock is released. Today a crash or deadline between the two saves leaves overflow sessions leased to a dead PID for about 2s, and overflow sessions are never marked in_flight.

title: ensure_reconciler_running() is called per session inside the Step A critical section and is not a singleton
plan_refs: §6.1 L728 (critical sections CPU-bounded, under 10ms); budget table L721 (one Popen at 20ms); §5.1 helper singleton
code_refs: handle_tab_closed L2768-2770 and handle_workspace_closed W38-40 (touch_reconciler_pending plus ensure_reconciler_running inside the with-block loop); ensure_reconciler_running L1194-1205 (unconditional Popen; no-op under HERDR_BARTENDER_UNIT_TESTING)
required_change: In Step A, collect a needs_reconciler flag and spawn once after the lock is released. Make ensure_reconciler_running check a reconciler singleton lock or PID file before Popen. Expose a test hook, such as a counter, so tests can assert that delegation happened instead of no-op'ing in tests.

title: Retryable failure of the inline cascade session does not hand off to the reconciler
plan_refs: §4.3 item 4 L568 (unconditional watchdog check); §5.2 L685; §6.1 L704
code_refs: handle_tab_closed L2836-2844 retryable branch; handle_workspace_closed same
required_change: After Step C, if any session in cache is not confirmed (retryable failure, attempts < 5, or a skipped send), call touch_reconciler_pending() and ensure_reconciler_running(). Today an Ended that fails with a network error is only retried on the next unrelated event.

title: Container matching is loose (suffix or substring) and falls back to the focused context
plan_refs: §2.1 L152-153 (cached tab_id/workspace_id matches the closed container); §11.1 L1344-1361 fixtures (tab_id 'w1:t1')

required_change: Match only on equality of canonical ids. If cached tab_ids may be unqualified, qualify both sides as f'{workspace_id}:{tab}' before comparing. Example: a cached tab 't1' in w1 matches a closed 'w2:t1'. Drop the f':{ws}:' in sid fallback, because it can match the host component of the sid. Also drop the context.tab_id/workspace_id fallback when event data lacks the id: the focused tab is not necessarily the closed one. Log and return instead.

required_change: Herdr envelopes carry agent_status/agent and never state=='Ended', so agent-exit envelopes are quarantined as status envelopes. Add a shared is_close_envelope(env) helper that returns True for pane/tab/workspace.closed, or for pane.agent_status_changed with agent_status=='idle' and not agent (Case B). Use it in _load, enqueue_spool and spool pruning. If the envelope cannot be parsed, keep it in spool/ rather than quarantining it, since a close cannot be ruled out.

That removes the hex marker and its .failed flag, matching the spec, while avoiding deletion of .va.tmp files and other unrelated entries. If the wholesale sweep is kept as defence-in-depth, also clear the .failed flags of salvaged panes.

Also cover the lease held by a live foreign PID, admission predating, and generation skip.

code_refs: run_unit_tests L4536-4547 (corrupt text uses 'herdr:macbook:...', but lookup uses host_test = get_sanitized_hostname(), and the asserts sit under 'if salvaged_sess:'); L3219-3229 does not check fields

code_refs: run_unit_tests sets PROCESS_DEADLINE_SECONDS=60 for the whole suite (L3082-3084); 'Bounded request timeout' test L3231-3237 only checks <1.0s with timeout=0.5
required_change: Add tests that patch START_TIME/PROCESS_DEADLINE_SECONDS to check the timeout formula at remaining 1.0/0.45/0.35/0.25s, including no POST when <=0.3. Call _timeout_watchdog directly with IN_CRITICAL_SECTION True and False. Create stale tmp files (os.utime -120s) and assert they are swept. Hold the orphan lock in a child process and assert the export returns within about 60ms and is deferred. Assert that pgrep runs at most once per 0.5s.

code_refs: run_unit_tests L3100-3113 (get_state_dir() without HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR override deletes the live active-sessions.json, panes and spool); export_orphan_record/remove_orphan_record default to Path.home()

title: Plan internal inconsistencies affecting this area
code_refs: enqueue_spool L1326-1334; handle_tab_closed L2763-2767; handle_workspace_closed
required_change: 1) The envelope payload key is 'data' at L390 but 'event_data' at L398 and L738. Recommend 'event_data', which the code and tests use. 2) Tombstone last_source_timestamp is the session value at L577, the event timestamp at L398, and 'ts' at L91; the code uses max(both). Recommend max(session.last_source_timestamp, event timestamp) as the most conservative choice against stale resurrection. 3) The generation check is 'ignore older than current generation' at L575 but strict equality at L397. Recommend skipping only when session.generation > envelope generation, so a close for a newer or equal turn still applies; the code already does this. 4) The budget table gives 150ms for lock acquisition while the formula allows 200ms; update the table to 200ms (the total becomes 1235ms, still under 1.5s). 5) Orphan lock: blocking per §4.3 vs LOCK_NB 50ms per §6.1. Recommend §6.1 for the plugin path.

title: Background reconciler inherits the 1.4s event-process deadline, so it takes cache locks with a 20ms budget, carries on without the lock, and uses 0.1s HTTP timeouts
plan_refs: L618 (exempt from 1.5s watchdog), L629-634 (long-lived loop), L683-686 (timeouts), L711-717
code_refs: time_remaining() L105-108; BoundedSessionCache.__enter__ L911-927 ('proceeding with best effort'); _raw_post_event L831; check_bridge_health L882; run_reconcile_background L1789 (never resets START_TIME/PROCESS_DEADLINE_SECONDS); main L5207
required_change: Add a background mode, set in main() before run_reconcile_background, --cleanup and --replay-orphans, that sets PROCESS_DEADLINE_SECONDS to infinity (or an explicit large budget) so time_remaining() no longer floors at 0.1. In background mode, BoundedSessionCache.__enter__ must wait with a bounded blocking timeout (for example 2s) and raise or skip the pass if it cannot get the lock. It must never return data unlocked. Event processes must also stop proceeding unlocked: on lock timeout they should go to the results/spool path (§4.3 L483). Bridge timeouts in background should use the 0.2s per-request value. Add a test that runs the reconciler more than 1.4s after START_TIME and asserts locked saves and 0.2s timeouts.

title: Reconciler is not started when an event leaves an active non-Ended session that was delivered, so the 20s marker heartbeat never runs
code_refs: handle_agent_status_changed L2394-2572 (should_spawn_reconciler is set only for undelivered, superseded or compensation cases); main L5216-5236 has no post-dispatch spawn
required_change: After Step C, if the cache still holds any non-Ended session (Working, Waiting, Idle or Done), call touch_reconciler_pending() and ensure_reconciler_running(). The singleton lock makes extra spawns harmless. Do the same at the end of the close handlers when sessions remain. Add a test that a delivered Working event starts a reconciler (mock Popen) and that the marker stays fresher than 60s across a simulated 90s pause.

title: Reconciler exits immediately when no delivered sessions exist, not after 60 idle seconds with zero sessions and a healthy bridge, and it ignores pending work
code_refs: run_reconcile_background L1924-1930; active_count L1851-1857 counts only delivered non-salvaged sessions
required_change: Track idle_since. Exit only when sessions, results/, spool/, pending_compensations, pending_vendor_cleanups and dismissed_vendor_uuids are all empty, DELIVERY_DOWN is absent and the last health probe succeeded, continuously for at least 60s. Undelivered in_flight sessions, non_retryable_failed sessions and salvaged sessions awaiting their 300s TTL must keep the loop alive. Make the sleep deadline min(20 or 300, next retry due, next dismissal due, next salvage expiry). Remove the redundant loop_once check at L1929.

title: Expiry of all sessions when Herdr has been dead for more than 5 minutes is not implemented
code_refs: reconcile_active_sessions L1618-1647 (no Herdr-dead timer); no herdr_dead_since field anywhere
required_change: Persist herdr_dead_since in the cache, set when get_herdr_pid() is None and cleared otherwise. title: stat -f %m tried first: on GNU stat it prints filesystem info, so the arithmetic fails and the vendor hook aborts with exit 1

code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender L353-354 HOOK_GUARD_TEMPLATE
required_change: With GNU coreutils stat (Linux, or macOS with Homebrew gnubin on PATH), `stat -f %m FILE` prints filesystem info to stdout and exits 1. The `||` chain then appends the output of `stat -c %Y`, so _HB_MARKER_MTIME becomes multi-line text that starts with 'File: ...'. The expression `$((_HB_NOW_TIME - _HB_MARKER_MTIME))` then fails under set -u. Reproduced in a sandbox: 'line 130: File: unbound variable', rc=1, and the vendor script never ran. So every hook call with a pane marker present kills the native vendor hook, which breaks fail-open. Fix (and update the plan block to match): run `stat -c %Y` first, because BSD stat fails cleanly with no stdout; fall back to `stat -f %m`; then check the value is numeric, e.g. `case $_HB_MARKER_MTIME in ''|*[!0-9]*) _HB_MARKER_MTIME=0;; esac`. Add a test that runs the guard against a fresh marker and asserts rc==0 on both platforms.

A missing or corrupt vendor-hook-sha.json, or a hook with no recorded SHA, is therefore auto-patched blindly. The plan says an unknown modification must block patching. Fail closed instead: no entry means HOOK_NEEDS_REVIEW. Also, the reconciler calls install_hooks(), which is the explicit-approval path. It rewrites the SHAs of all hooks (silently approving upstream changes to hooks whose guard is still present) and unlinks HOOK_NEEDS_REVIEW and .hook_review_alerted. Split this into a non-approving `repair_hooks(names)` that only re-inserts the guard into hooks whose clean SHA matches, never updates vendor-hook-sha.json, and never clears review flags. install_hooks(approve=True) stays the CLI path. title: Insert adds '\n' around the guard but strip removes only the markers, so the round trip is not byte-exact
plan_refs: §7.3 L1062 (clean SHA), L1065 (.pristine), L1072 (strip cleanly); §9.1 L1146-1147 (different strip algorithm)
code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender L564-566, L588-591, L607 (f"\n{HOOK_GUARD_TEMPLATE}\n"), L665 uninstall strip, L1897-1898 reconciler strip
required_change:
Verified: patching '#!/bin/bash
set -u
echo hi
' and then stripping gives '...set -u


echo hi
', with 2 extra newlines. Consequences: (1) uninstall does not restore the original bytes; (2) a second --install-hooks stores the SHA of the stripped content, not the pristine one, so a later vendor revert to the original script triggers a false HOOK_NEEDS_REVIEW; (3) .pristine is overwritten with the drifted content on every reinstall (L582-584). Write a single pair of helpers, insert_guard() and strip_guard(), shared by install, uninstall and the reconciler, with strip_guard(insert_guard(x)) == x. For example, insert the exact text TEMPLATE+'
' and strip with the regex `(?s)
?# BEGIN ...?# END HERDR-BARTENDER DEDUP GUARD
` that matches what was inserted. Read and write in binary mode (or newline='') so CRLF and non-UTF-8 bytes are preserved, and hash the bytes. Align the §9.1 inline python strip with the same algorithm. Add a round-trip test.

If it contains BEGIN without END, verify_vendor_hooks_intact reports it missing, and the install else-branch inserts a second guard, so the file then has 2 BEGINs. Require count(BEGIN)==1, count(END)==1 and BEGIN before END. Otherwise, in install, uninstall and the reconciler, abort without touching the file, log the problem and (in the reconciler) touch HOOK_NEEDS_REVIEW. Add tests for both cases.

title: Root cause of the Linux --unit-test failure at L3601: the hook guard's stat fallback breaks on GNU coreutils and kills the vendor hook (rc=1)
code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender L352 `_HB_MARKER_MTIME=$(stat -f %m "$_HB_PANE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y ... || echo 0)`; L353-354 arithmetic; failing assert L3601 (test #23 Step D, `assert res.returncode == 0`)
required_change: I confirmed this in a sandbox: I copied the template to scratch and set HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR to a tempdir. On GNU, `stat -f` means filesystem mode, so `stat -f %m FILE` prints multi-line filesystem info to stdout for FILE. It then exits 1 because '%m' is not a file. The `||` fallback appends the `stat -c %Y` output to the same capture. Under `set -u`, `$((_HB_NOW_TIME - _HB_MARKER_MTIME))` then aborts with 'File: unbound variable', so the hook exits 1 and the vendor script never runs (it fails closed). This happens whenever a pane marker exists and the flags are clear, which breaks tests #23D, #52, #55, #61 (third case), #62 and #67 on Linux. It is also a production bug on macOS for anyone with Homebrew coreutils gnubin on PATH. Fix: try GNU first and validate the result: `_HB_MARKER_MTIME=$(stat -c %Y "$f" 2>/dev/null) || _HB_MARKER_MTIME=$(stat -f %m "$f" 2>/dev/null) || _HB_MARKER_MTIME=0; case $_HB_MARKER_MTIME in ''|*[!0-9]*) _HB_MARKER_MTIME=0;; esac`. Once the stat fix is in, PASSTHROUGH vs suppress still depends on a real `herdr` process existing (`pgrep -f Herdr.app || pgrep -xi herdr`, L354). This host passed only because herdr happens to be running, so a pgrep PATH shim is needed (see harness gap). Add a regression test that runs the guard with a fresh marker and asserts rc==0 under both a GNU-style and a BSD-style stat shim.

required_change: Send a status for a pane with no agent field and no existing session, and assert no session is created and no POST is made. Then for an admitted session, send agent: None and separately agent: '', and assert an Ended POST reaches the mock and the session is evicted.

title: #6 does not simulate Ended in flight in the drain loop
code_refs: L3191-3208 (Ended fails with 500, then Working arrives sequentially; only desired_state is asserted)
required_change: Block the mock on the Ended POST using a gate Event. While it is blocked, deliver a Working event from another thread or process, then release. Assert the session is not deleted from the cache and that the mock received Working after Ended (final mock state Working).

title: #7 does not check that seq increases monotonically
code_refs: L3171-3189 asserts only seq>=1
required_change: Send N events and record seq after each one. Assert they strictly increase by 1 for accepted events, and that the payload seq sent to the mock is also strictly increasing.

title: #9 tests marker helpers directly instead of the delivery, close and heartbeat paths
required_change: Assert the marker appears after a confirmed handle_agent_status_changed delivery and not after a 500. Assert it is removed after handle_pane_closed. Age it with os.utime and assert run_reconcile_background(loop_once=True) refreshes its mtime.

title: #10 spool FIFO order is not asserted
code_refs: L3241-3274 counts delivered events only
required_change: Write envelopes with out-of-order filenames and arrival times. Assert that the mock history order matches FIFO by filename or arrival, and that superseded (older-seq) envelopes are dropped.

title: #11 does not verify that new work is completed or the fixed backoff
code_refs: L3276-3287 only checks that reconciler.pending is touched and unlinked
required_change: Seed an undelivered session and touch reconciler.pending, then run without loop_once and with an injected sleep. Assert the loop re-scans and delivers before exiting. Assert retry sleeps follow 0/1/2/4/8s through a patched time.sleep recorder.

title: #12 does not assert salvage invariants or signal safety
required_change: After quarantine, assert the salvaged record has seq==delivered_seq, desired_state!='Ended', salvaged True and delivery_status 'salvaged', that the mock received no POST for it on the next reconcile, and that the .corrupt.<timestamp> name matches the pattern. For signal safety, set IN_CRITICAL_SECTION=True, send SIGALRM through _timeout_watchdog, and assert PENDING_WATCHDOG_EXIT is set with no exit. Alternatively, run a subprocess with a tiny deadline and assert the cache is never left half-written.

title: #14 DISABLED test checks only is_disabled()
required_change: Run the plugin as a subprocess with DISABLED present and an event env set, and assert exit 0, no POST and no cache mutation. Run `--cleanup` with DISABLED present and assert it still sends Ended and returns 0.

title: #17 does not drive failures through delivery
code_refs: L3394-3404 calls touch/clear helpers directly
required_change: Make the mock return 500 three times across three events. Assert .failed exists after the first, DELIVERY_DOWN is absent after two and present after three, and consecutive_failures is tracked. Then a 200 clears both.

title: #30 does not assert that the vendor dismissal is sent outside the lock
code_refs: L3814-3835 (the _raw_post_event raise under UNIT_TESTING at L822-825 is an implicit oracle only)
required_change: Record the IN_CRITICAL_SECTION value in the mock handler (same process) or patch _raw_post_event with a recorder. Explicitly assert it was False for the vendor-UUID Ended POST, and that the dismissal was staged in the cache under lock first.

title: #31 and #37 parity tests run a hand-copied bash snippet, not HOOK_GUARD_TEMPLATE
code_refs: L3837-3863, L4158-4185 (inline bash duplicates template L229-238)
required_change: Run the actual guard in fall-through mode (herdr-unhealthy shim). Read back which panes/<hex>.vendor_active filename it created, and compare it with get_hex_pane_id(normalize_pane_id(raw, ws)). Use an exhaustive fixture table: 48-char limit, 49 chars rejected, invalid chars, multi-colon, empty workspace, colon-less without workspace rejected (no file created).

title: #33 terminal-event matrix is incomplete
code_refs: L3887-3918 covers only Done and Ended in argv; the 'condition 3 fails' sub-case uses Ended, which always passes, so it proves nothing
required_change: Parameterize over {Stop, Done, AgentDone, AgentWaiting, agent-turn-complete} (expect pass-through, .vendor_active retained) and {Ended, SessionEnd, session-end} (expect pass-through, .vendor_active removed). Cover each delivery mode: argv token, stdin JSON hook_event_name and argv JSON. Run each under both healthy and unhealthy Herdr shims.

title: #35 does not test dropping older-generation spool events
required_change: Patch time.time to step backward after admission. Enqueue a spool envelope carrying the older generation and replay it. Assert it is dropped and that generation and cache_seq strictly increase.

title: #44 does not cover lock or state isolation across workspaces
required_change: Admit w1:p1 and w2:p1 and assert two distinct session IDs, hex_w1 != hex_w2, and independent markers. Close w1 and assert the w2 session, marker and .vendor_active are untouched.

title: #45 does not test bare-touch preservation past 60s
code_refs: L4398-4414 tests only the unlink paths
required_change: Age the bare-touch .vendor_active to 120s with os.utime while the session is active, run a reconcile pass, and assert the file still exists (no blind expiry). Then pane close removes it.

title: Stdin-capture timing bounds are looser than the spec, and the remainder splice is not verified
code_refs: #46 L4416-4449 asserts <2.5s; #56 L4670-4701 writes one line and never sends a remainder
required_change: #46: assert elapsed <= 1.0s plus a small tolerance (e.g. <1.5s) and rc 0. #56: the writer sends line 1, sleeps 1.5s (past the alarm), then sends line 2 and closes. Run the vendor as `cat` and assert stdout == line1+line2 byte-for-byte, that the guard returned control within 2.0s, and that no .guard_splice.* or .guard_stdin.* remains.

title: #50 salvage assertions are conditional and keyed to the wrong host
code_refs: L4516-4552: the corrupt cache uses 'herdr:macbook:...', the lookup uses host_test, and the checks sit under `if salvaged_sess:`, so they are skipped
required_change: Use the same session ID for the seed and the lookup, and assert unconditionally: salvaged is True, desired_state and delivered_state are 'Idle', delivery_status is 'salvaged', and generation >= 1_700_000_000. Assert all pane markers were removed and that no POST was sent for salvaged sessions on the next reconcile.

title: #54 does not test the re-verification abort or forced re-sync branches
required_change: Add cases where (a) the compensation target was re-admitted with a fresh session, so assert no Ended is sent and the entry is purged, and (b) a race happens during the send through a mock gate, so assert delivered_seq is reset to 0 and status is in_flight. Also assert that an Ended was actually sent for the plain case (mock history).

title: #60 covers only the .vendor_active cancellation trigger
code_refs: L4805-4824; HERDR_BARTENDER_UNIT_TESTING forces is_herdr_alive() True (L211-213), so the herdr-dead trigger cannot be tested
required_change: Parameterize over each trigger (.vendor_active, .failed, DISABLED, NO_HOOKS, herdr dead via a pgrep shim or injectable liveness). Assert the entry is purged and no Ended is sent. Replace the env-var short-circuit in is_herdr_alive with the PATH shim so tests can drive both states.

title: #65 does not test the 2.0s interval gate or the 5-attempt cap, and its comment follows the stale 3-attempt reading
code_refs: L4970-5000 (the comment says 'attempts 1 (< 3)'); code L1549-1568 uses 5
required_change: With a frozen clock: (a) last_attempt 1.0s ago gives no POST and attempts unchanged; (b) 2.0s ago gives a POST and attempts+1; (c) attempts==5 gives a purge without POST; (d) age >=10s gives a purge; (e) a confirmed 200 gives a purge (code currently retains on 200 within the window; confirm that against the spec). Fix the comment.

title: Minor weak assertions in #1, #19, #57 and #62
code_refs: #1 L3116-3119 (no 'port' check); #19 L3420-3448 (UUID dismissal Ended POST not asserted); #57 L4703-4736 (Idle only, not Done); #62 L4861-4878 (closed pipe only, no TTY case)
required_change: #1: assert health['port']==mock_port. #19: assert the mock history contains {state: Ended, session_id: 'test_v_uuid_123'}. #57: add a Done session. #62: run the guard with stdin attached to a pty (pty.openpty) and no argv, and assert PASSTHROUGH within 1s.

title: Guard and Python liveness checks depend on real host processes (herdr, Bartender) and on platform tools
code_refs: guard L354 `pgrep -f "Herdr.app" || pgrep -xi herdr` (the -f form also false-matches any cmdline containing 'Herdr.app'); get_herdr_pid L176 `pgrep -xi` + `ps -o comm=`; get_bartender_pid L1458 `pgrep -x 'Bartender 6'`; get_process_start_time L63 `ps -o lstart=` parsed with a locale-dependent strptime; osascript L1916; perl/python3 capture L279-288; is_herdr_alive short-circuited by HERDR_BARTENDER_UNIT_TESTING L211
required_change: Provide test PATH shims for pgrep, ps, osascript and stat (GNU- and BSD-flavored), controlled by files in the sandbox: e.g. shims/state/herdr_pids, bartender_pids, lstart.<pid>, and osascript writes calls to a log. procps-ng pgrep 4.0.4 here does support -x and -i, so the flags are not the problem; process presence is. Make the guard pgrep pattern anchored (e.g. `pgrep -f '/Herdr\.app/Contents/MacOS/'`) to avoid self-matches. Remove the UNIT_TESTING liveness short-circuit in favor of the shims so Herdr-dead paths become testable.

title: §10.2 injectable clock is not implemented
code_refs: No clock abstraction. time.time()/time.time_ns()/time.monotonic() are called directly throughout. Tests only back-date last_event_at (L3313-3353) and use os.utime once (#57 L4710). Module globals PROCESS_ARRIVAL_TIME/_NS (L55-57) are frozen at import.
required_change: Add a `FakeClock` test fixture that patches time.time, time.time_ns, time.monotonic and time.sleep in the loaded module namespace (the module imports `time`, so patch `mod.time` with a shim object or use unittest.mock.patch.object on time functions within a context). The fixture should support advance() and step_back(). Use it for exact boundary tests: TTLs, the 12h absence horizon, the 300s salvage horizon, lease deadline +0.5s grace rows (which currently rely on real-time sleeps in the #34 Row 4/5 offsets), the settling window and retry backoff.

title: §10.2 multi-process harness does not exist; every race test is sequential and in-process
code_refs: run_unit_tests L3080-5081 calls handlers in one process. Lease rows simulate other holders by editing the cache. The only real foreign process is `sleep 30` (L3946).
required_change: Build a harness that (1) spawns N copies of bin/herdr-bartender with HERDR_PLUGIN_EVENT, HERDR_PLUGIN_EVENT_JSON and HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON set and a sandboxed env, against (2) a mock bridge with per-request gates and an ordered log, with barrier-style release. Then assert the final cache and the bridge state. Required scenarios: concurrent close vs status, concurrent senders on one pane (lease), hung sender (SIGSTOP/SIGCONT a child to force takeover), deadline exit under a delayed bridge, and the reconciler singleton under concurrent spawn.

title: §10.2 `--live-test` flag is not recognized; code uses `--test` and the live test does not verify outcomes
code_refs: main L5149 `if "--test" in args`; README L55 documents --test; run_live_test L5084-5139 only prints and never asserts that /health sessions return to 0. Running `--live-test` today silently falls through to normal event dispatch and exits 0 with no output.
required_change: Accept `--live-test`, keeping `--test` as an alias. Record health['sessions'] before and after, and assert the post-Ended count equals the baseline (or 0). Exit non-zero on failure, then update the README. Document live checklist items 2-3 (Herdr symlink, vendor handover via killall herdr) as a scripted or manual procedure in docs, optionally with a `--live-test --handover` interactive mode.

title: Suite is one 2,000-line function with bare asserts that stops on first failure, and tests depend on each other's leftover state
code_refs: run_unit_tests L3080-5081. Bare asserts are stripped under `python -O`. #3 depends on the session count from #2 (L3164). Earlier sections leave sessions behind (e.g. 'herdr:macbook:*'). server.shutdown is only reached on success (L5080). Plan items 1-23 do not line up with the code's section numbers (code #13/#14 cover plan #15, code #16 is extra, plan #4 has no section).
required_change: Move to stdlib unittest under tests/, one file per area: test_bridge_contract, test_lifecycle, test_cascades_tombstones, test_generations_ordering, test_spool, test_cache_salvage, test_leases, test_reconciler, test_orphans_cleanup, test_hook_guard, test_install_hooks, test_parity, test_multiprocess. Base TestCase setUp gives a fresh sandbox (HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR, PATH shims, env scrub) and loads the script with importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader('herdr_bartender', 'bin/herdr-bartender'). Note that import runs `ps` at module load (L72 PROCESS_START_TIME), so the shims must be in place first. A class-level mock bridge fixture uses a scripted response queue, gate Events and a full request log including failed requests. Use self.assert* everywhere and name each test after its plan number (test_p23_...). `--unit-test` should run `unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover(<repo>/tests)` and exit with that status, falling back to an error if tests/ is missing. Helpers worth keeping and moving into tests/support: MockBartenderHandler (extend it), the 'guard template + echo SENTINEL' script builder, the FIFO stalled-writer pattern from #46/#56, the `sleep 30` live-PID plus get_process_start_time lease fixture, direct cache seeding via `with BoundedSessionCache(...) as data: ...; save()`, os.utime marker aging, run_reconcile_background(loop_once=True), the reject_complex_ended flag, ensure_reconciler_running being a no-op under the test env, and the _raw_post_event IN_CRITICAL_SECTION raise as an invariant oracle.

title: Plan says '60 core invariants' but lists 68
code_refs: n/a
required_change: Change the plan to '68'. All 68 are normative, and items 61-68 are referenced elsewhere in the spec.

title: Plan disagrees on the dismissal retry cap (3 vs 5) and on the purge criteria
plan_refs: §5.1 L645 ('3 attempts') vs L646, §1 L43, L56, §10.1 #65 L1268 ('5 attempts'); L43/L56 example schedule t=0,2,4,6,8,10 is 6 sends; L56 adds a purge if age >60s
code_refs: reconciler L1549-1568 uses 5 attempts and 10s, with no 60s age purge visible; test #65 comment L4984 uses the 3 reading
required_change: Treat 5 attempts, a 2.0s interval and a 10s window as authoritative: it appears in 4 places, matches the code and is what #65 asserts. Delete L645, change the example schedule to t=0,2,4,6,8 (5 sends), and either implement and test the 60s age purge from L56 or remove it from the plan.

title: pgrep/ps liveness probes run with no subprocess timeout on the watchdog-bounded hot path
plan_refs: plan §6.1 L700-706 (bounded operations), budget table L712 (liveness check worst case 35ms), §1 L135 (liveness gate before every send)
code_refs: bin/herdr-bartender get_process_start_time L63, get_herdr_pid L176 and L185, get_bartender_pid L1458: subprocess.run(...) without timeout=. get_bartender_pid is called from _raw_post_event L827 on every send, PROCESS_START_TIME forks ps at import (L76), and is_process_instance_alive forks ps inside the Step A critical section
required_change: Pass timeout=0.1 (or min(0.1, time_remaining()-0.3)) to every ps/pgrep call and catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired. On timeout, treat the result as unknown: the liveness gate returns 'unknown, defer to reconciler' and the start time is None, never a fabricated value. Also run ps with env LC_ALL=C. Combine this with the 0.5s memo the liveness-cache gap already requires. Add a test where a PATH shim makes pgrep sleep 5s and assert that the handler process still exits within 1.5s.

title: BoundedSessionCache.save() swallows write failures, so callers send over the network on a lease/seq that was never persisted
plan_refs: plan §6.2 L730-733 (every mutation is atomically persisted), §4.3 Step A then B ordering (lease claim persisted before transmission), user rule 'never silently swallow errors'
code_refs: save() L1096-1164: `except Exception as e: log_debug(...)` returns normally; tmp_path is left behind; every handler then proceeds to post_bartender_event (e.g. handle_agent_status_changed L2392-2396) as if the lease, seq and desired_payload were on disk
required_change: Make save() raise a CacheWriteError (or return False). Unlink tmp_path on failure. In Step A, a failed save must abort the send path: enqueue to the spool if possible, touch reconciler.pending and exit 0. In Step C, a failed save must write a results/ envelope so the confirmation is not lost. Add a test that makes the state dir read-only (or monkeypatches os.replace to raise) and asserts that no POST was made and that a spool or results file or log line exists.

title: cleanup_vendor_active sends the vendor Ended before staging the dismissal in cache, the reverse of the stage-then-dispatch rule
plan_refs: plan §1 L9 (dismissals are staged under lock and dispatched outside the lock), L56 (record uuid with attempts:1 and last_attempt), §5.1 5a/5b
code_refs: cleanup_vendor_active L751-791: _raw_post_event first, then unlink .vendor_active, then a separate lock to add dismissed_vendor_uuids[v_sid] without attempts/last_attempt; all exceptions are swallowed
required_change: Under the cache lock, first record dismissed_vendor_uuids[uuid] = {timestamp, pane_hex, attempts: 0, last_attempt: 0}. Release the lock, then POST (budget-gated by time_remaining() > 0.3). Then re-lock and set attempts=1 and last_attempt, and purge the entry on ok:true. Only after the entry is recorded may .vendor_active be unlinked. If the process is killed between the send and the record, the reconciler then still owns the retry. Add a test that kills the process (raises SystemExit) right after the POST and asserts the dismissal survives in the cache.

title: SIGALRM handler does unlocked cache reads, log I/O and a raw Popen that skips the singleton or unit-test guard; its spawn criterion differs from the spec
plan_refs: plan §3.4 L245 (handler sets PENDING_WATCHDOG_EXIT, zero file I/O in handler context; outside critical sections, a non-blocking helper spawn then exit 0), §6.1 L727-729
code_refs: _timeout_watchdog L111-134: log_debug (which may rotate the log), open and json.load of active-sessions.json without the lock, subprocess.Popen directly (not ensure_reconciler_running, so the HERDR_BARTENDER_UNIT_TESTING no-op is skipped), spawn only if delivered_seq<seq or Ended, ignoring pending_compensations, pending_vendor_cleanups, spool and results
required_change: Reduce the handler to: set PENDING_WATCHDOG_EXIT=True; if IN_CRITICAL_SECTION, return; otherwise touch reconciler.pending (a single open/close, or os.utime), call ensure_reconciler_running() and os._exit(0) (or sys.exit(0)). The spawn decision belongs to the reconciler, which exits on its own when there is nothing to do. Add a test that calls _timeout_watchdog with IN_CRITICAL_SECTION False and asserts exactly one spawn request through the test hook, with no cache read.

title: handle_pane_closed matches sessions by sid suffix, so closing w1:p1 also closes a multi-colon pane x:w1:p1
plan_refs: plan §2.1 L151 (evict the matching pane session), PANE_ID regex allows multi-colon IDs (L15)
code_refs: handle_pane_closed L2597 and L2609: `info.get('pane_id') == canonical_pane or sid.endswith(f':{canonical_pane}')`
required_change: Match only on equality: info.get('pane_id') == canonical_pane, or sid == f"herdr:{data['host']}:{canonical_pane}". Add a regression test with the sessions w1:p1 and x:w1:p1 where closing w1:p1 leaves x:w1:p1 intact. This is separate from the auditors' tab and workspace loose-match finding.

title: save() reads ~/.herdr-bartender-orphans.json inside the cache critical section without the orphan lock
plan_refs: plan §1 L108 (orphan file operations are executed strictly OUTSIDE the cache lock, <10ms CPU bound), §5.1 item 12, L107 (pane_generations prune protects orphan-referenced keys)
code_refs: BoundedSessionCache.save L1129-1145 (json.load of the orphan file during the 512-cap prune, path hard-coded via Path.home())
required_change: Compute the protected orphan pane set outside the lock: read it under the orphan lock before entering the cache lock, or persist an 'orphan_panes' set in the cache whenever export_orphan_record or remove_orphan_record runs. Pass that set into the prune. Resolve the orphan path through the shared get_orphan_path() so tests can sandbox it.

title: Manifest [[events]] commands do not pass the event name, so the spec's argv fallback cannot work
plan_refs: plan §3.4 L243 (invoked as ./bin/herdr-bartender <event_name>; argv ${1:-} fallback when stdin is empty or malformed)
code_refs: herdr-plugin.toml [[events]] command = ["./bin/herdr-bartender"] for all four events; main() L5213 never reads argv[1]
required_change: Confirm whether Herdr appends the event name to the command. If it does not, set the command per event, e.g. ["./bin/herdr-bartender", "pane.closed"]. Pair this with the main-stdin-envelope fix so that argv[1], when it is not a flag, is the fallback event name. Add a manifest lint test asserting that each [[events]] entry's command, plus the event name, resolves to a known handler.
